title: Australia Travel Guide
summary: A concise Australia travel guide for nature lovers, coastal explorers, and city travellers who want the best of down under.
bestTime: September–November and March–May for mild weather, fewer crowds, and ideal outdoor conditions.

quickFacts.Visa: eVisitor/ETA required for most travellers; apply before departure.

attractions.name: Sydney
attractions.summary: Opera House, Harbour Bridge, coastal walks, and vibrant dining.

attractions.name: Great Barrier Reef
attractions.summary: World’s largest coral reef system with snorkeling and diving experiences.

attractions.name: Melbourne
attractions.summary: Cultural capital with laneways, cafés, and art festivals.

attractions.name: Uluru
attractions.summary: Red centre icon with sunsets, indigenous culture, and desert walks.

attractions.name: Great Ocean Road
attractions.summary: Scenic coastal drive with dramatic cliffs, beaches, and wildlife.

cultureEtiquette: Be punctual for tours and guided activities.
Respect indigenous cultural sites and follow park guidelines.
Tip when service is exceptional, but it is not always expected.
gettingAround: Use domestic flights for long distances between major regions.
Rent a car for the Great Ocean Road and rural national parks.
Take trams and trains in Melbourne, and ferries in Sydney.

itineraries.title: Reef Adventure
activities: Take a Great Barrier Reef day trip

sustainability: Respect reef and marine life guidelines while snorkeling.
Use public transit in cities and reduce single-use plastic.
Support eco-friendly wildlife sanctuaries and tours.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for Australia?
faqs.a: Yes, most international visitors must obtain an ETA or visitor visa before travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Australia?
faqs.a: Spring and autumn offer the best weather for outdoor travel without peak-season crowds.
Australia is generally high-cost, so book accommodation and activities early to lock in savings.
